question.problem:
Using the trapezoidal rule with the partition

$$
[0,5]=[0,2]\cup [2,5],
$$

approximate the area under the curve of the continuous function $y=f(x)$ whose data is given in the table below.

| $x$ | $0$ | $2$ | $5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $3$ | $1$ | $4$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let's plot what this function might look like, using the values given in the table.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14274355/assets/3421933d57ba9341f1743ecc47507966f91d1d7c134d194cbe5bc5d9ef51fadd.png)

We've drawn some trapezoids to help calculate our trapezoidal rule sum. By calculating the area of each trapezoid, we obtain the following approximation for our area $A:$

$$
A≈\overset{1\text{st trapezoid}}{\overset{⏞}{[\,\frac{\overset{\text{bases}}{\overset{⏞}{f(0)+f(2)}}}{2}\,\cdot \,{{Δ{x}_{1}}_{⏟}}_{\text{height}}\,]}}+\overset{2\text{nd trapezoid}}{\overset{⏞}{[\,\frac{\overset{\text{bases}}{\overset{⏞}{f(2)+f(5)}}}{2}\,\cdot \,{{Δ{x}_{2}}_{⏟}}_{\text{height}}\,]}}
$$

Substituting the appropriate numbers into the above expression gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈\frac{3+1}{2}\cdot (2-0)+\frac{1+4}{2}\cdot (5-2) \\  & =2\cdot 2+\frac{5}{2}\cdot 3 \\  & =4+\frac{15}{2} \\  & =\frac{23}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
